about: W2, The cut (for-review/design/faction-quests.md, 2.2). The Wardens' weekly cut from the three named bars of Rotgut Row: twelve litres each. Tarp Nine has nothing: its tin was taken in the night, by the Warden who stands the wagon lane at the gate. Marks: w2 (2 on the Row, 100 done), w2.sump and w2.det (1 paid), w2.fen (1 Fen has been asked), w2.nine (how Tarp Nine's twelve was come by: 1 squeezed out of Fen's stock, 2 put in by the player, 3 got back from the Warden who took it), w2.cut (litres carried for the post), w2.asked (Fen asked who), w2.knows (Mash has said who), w2.told (the Warden was told Rook would hear), w2.split (the player took half to keep quiet), w2.kept (skimmed), lanewarden.sold (he is sentenced by his own desk, and is on the Block), fen.gone (Tarp Nine has changed hands), fen.bed (a cot behind the tarp is the player's), coat (a Warden's coat on loan: nothing reads it yet). Rook gives it at the tally desk, as in W1.
name: The cut
giver: Sergeant Rook, at the tally desk in the Gate Yard
steps: Collect twelve litres from each of the three bars of Rotgut Row: The Sump, Tarp Nine and Detention. The Row is west off the end of Pool Street, under the overpass. Then take the count back to Rook.
The Row's cut was taken to Rook.

Sergeant Rook.words: The Row's cut is due tonight, and the bars know every face on my shift. They do not know yours. Three bars, twelve litres each: The Sump, Tarp Nine, Detention. Thirty-six comes back to this desk. Forty-five for the walk.
Up Main Street, through the square, up the lane to Pool Street, and west off the end of it under the overpass. The furrow the airliner left. You will smell it before you see it.
Thirty-six. If a bar is short, it is short: bring me what there is and tell me which. What the post does about a short bar is the post's business, not yours.
Sergeant Rook.log: Took the Wardens' cut to collect from the three bars of Rotgut Row.

Sergeant Rook.words: Three bars. I will hear the count when you have been to all three, and not a count of two.

answers.words: Thirty-six. And Tarp Nine's twelve came out of your own man's vest: the one on the wagon lane.
Twenty-four. Tarp Nine's tin was taken in the night, and it has nothing.
Twenty-four. Tarp Nine was robbed, and by your own man on the wagon lane.
They were all short tonight. Twenty-one.
answers.log: Told Rook the Row was short, and kept 15 L of the cut.

Sergeant Rook.words: Thirty-six. Forty-five for the walk, and a coat off the peg. Wear it and half this town looks straight through you.
Sergeant Rook.log: Brought Rook the whole of the Row's cut. He paid 45 L and lent a Warden's coat.

Sergeant Rook.words: Off my own shift. Nine years on that lane. He will be on the Block before the week is out, and what he took goes back where it came from. Forty-five, the coat, and I do not forget who told me.
Sergeant Rook.log: Told Rook which of his own Wardens robbed Tarp Nine. The man is to be sold at the Block.

Sergeant Rook.words: Then Tarp Nine has a new keeper by the end of the week. That is not a threat. It is the Row. Forty-five was for thirty-six: it is thirty for twenty-four.
Sergeant Rook.log: Brought Rook 24 L of the Row's 36. Tarp Nine was short, and changes hands.

Sergeant Rook.words: Twenty-one. From three bars that have never once been short together. Stand there.
I had a runner up the Row before you were back down it. They paid thirty-six. Put the fifteen on the desk. You are finished at this post until I say you are not.
Sergeant Rook.log: Rook had the Row counted behind me. He took the 15 L back, and I am not welcome at the post.

Sergeant Rook.words: Twenty-one, then. Short weeks happen. Forty-five for the walk.
Sergeant Rook.log: Rook took 21 L for the Row's cut and paid 45 L for the walk.

Sergeant Rook.words: Captain Voss wants a man brought in from the Bones. That is his to ask, not mine, and he does his asking at a back table in the Velvet Tin. Not tonight.
You counted my water short to my face. The lane is that way, and the street is the other.

Lane Warden.words: Fen's tin. You have been talking to the bus. All right. It was sitting there, and a fence's tin is nobody's water.

answers.words: Hand over the twelve. It goes back in the cut, and nobody hears.
answers.log: Got Tarp Nine's twelve litres back from the Warden who took it.

answers.words: Rook will hear it from me.
Six to me, and I was never down this lane.
answers.log: Took 6 L from the Warden who robbed Tarp Nine, to say nothing.

Lane Warden.words: Twelve. Count it. And you were never down this lane.
Then he hears it. I have stood this lane nine years, and I will stand it tomorrow.
Six. A pleasure. Now go and be somewhere else.

Big Lottie.words: The post's cut, and a new face to carry it. Twelve. Count it where I can see you count it.
Tell your sergeant The Sump has never once been short. And when you get up the Row, look at who is.

Mash.words: Twelve, on the counter. Detention pays on the night. I cannot afford a Warden who does not like me.
You will find Tarp Nine lighter than you want it. That was not Fen's doing.

Who robbed Fen? I see the whole west lip from this bus, and I do not sleep. Boots, not sandals. A vest with plates in it. Heavy, and breathing like the walk up the cut was the most he had done all week. Whoever stands at your gate with nothing to do.
Mash.log: Mash saw who took Tarp Nine's tin: a heavy Warden in a plate vest, off the gate.

Fen.words: The cut. Yes. Somebody came down off the lip in the night and took the tin, and what was in the tin, and the cut was in the tin. I have stock. I have no water.

answers.words: I will put your twelve in myself. (12 L)
answers.log: Put 12 L of my own into the Wardens' cut for Tarp Nine.

answers.words: Then your stock goes in the furrow, jar by jar, until twelve litres turns up.
answers.log: Broke Fen's stock at Tarp Nine until the cut was paid.

answers.words: Then the post hears Tarp Nine is short.

Fen.words: Somebody who knew which night the tin was full. Ask Mash. She sees this lip from the bus, and she does not sleep.
Nobody does that. Not on this Row. There is a cot behind the tarp: if you ever need not to be found for a night, it is yours.
Stop. Stop. Here. That was to buy next week's stock. You have closed Tarp Nine a week early, and you may tell your sergeant so.
Mash told me who, and that you got it out of him. So the post robs me at night and collects from me in the morning. Still. You did not have to.
The cot is behind the tarp. Nobody asks at Tarp Nine. That is the whole trade.

people.name: A new keeper
people.prompt: Talk to whoever has Tarp Nine now

lines.words: Fen? Fen lost the pitch. The post said short, and the Row heard it. I pay three tenths, not four, and the cup is what it costs now.

people.name: A Warden, sentenced
people.prompt: Talk to the Warden in the collar

lines.words: Nine years on that lane. They read me my own sentence off my own desk. Do you know what a Warden fetches on that Block? Everybody he ever fined is going to bid.
